questions: Should the series length be exactly the number of days in the range (i.e., (end_date - start_date).days) or should it be the number of days inclusive (i.e., (end_date - start_date).days + 1)?
When start_date equals end_date, should the series contain a single element (that date) or be empty?
Should the random dates be generated with replacement (allowing duplicates) or without replacement (ensuring uniqueness)?
Should the output series have a specific index (e.g., default RangeIndex) or should it be indexed by the generated dates?
Should the random dates be uniformly distributed across the inclusive range, or is any distribution acceptable?
Should the function handle time components (hours, minutes, seconds) in the datetime objects, or should it ignore them and only consider dates?
If seed is None, should the random number generator be left unseeded (non-reproducible) or should it use a default seed?
Should the function accept datetime.date objects in addition to datetime.datetime objects?
